provider-truth.instructions: Start from current providerContracts, the provider, DevOps and secret-manager registries, and the OpenTofu engine implementation within the shard's declared scope; do not audit only the best-documented providers. For every claim, distinguish schema/registry presence, implemented adapter behavior, mocked safety and lifecycle coverage, current official provider documentation, and successful live-conformance evidence. Repository prose, implementation notes, metadata, and mocked tests are claims rather than independent proof. A ready-for-live or planned capability must not be described publicly as supported. A supported claim without concrete linked or committed live-conformance evidence from the last 90 days is a finding; never infer a live pass from test code. Verify provider API behavior only through current official documentation on the allowlisted hosts and include exact source URLs in evidence. If required official documentation cannot be reached, set complete=false and report the source gap. Compare the public website and docs with test/provider-conformance/provider-matrix.ts, current registry metadata, adapter ports, engine workflows, focused tests, and live harness coverage. Report contradictions, missing lifecycle layers, stale evidence, undocumented limitations, and claims broader than the implemented or verified contract. Do not mutate resources, run opt-in live tests, use provider credentials, edit files, or promote statuses.

shards.instructions: Audit current registered hosting capabilities and the OpenTofu-managed compute lifecycle for GCP, AWS and Azure, plus retained Railway workflows. Derive the resource and capability inventory from the current provider registry and engine implementation. Cover cloud access and setup, project and service identity, deploy sources and managed CI recipes, runtime and environment wiring, maintenance, custom domains, teardown, mocked contracts, recent live evidence, and public support claims. Leave data resources and integrations to their assigned shards.

Audit current registered DNS, domain and edge capabilities and implemented repository Pages routing. Derive the inventory from current provider registrations and shared workflows. Cover durable identity, routing, maintenance, certificates and domains, DNS ownership, teardown, mocked contracts, recent live evidence, and public support claims. Leave compute hosting and code-host collaboration to their assigned shards.

Audit current registered database, cache, storage, queue, resilience, restore-drill, and data-migration capabilities and the corresponding OpenTofu-managed resources for GCP, AWS and Azure, plus retained Railway workflows. Derive the resource inventory from current provider registrations and the engine implementation. Cover private creation, scoped identity, observation, runtime wiring, data-plane behavior, retry-safe teardown, mocked contracts, recent live evidence, and public support claims.

Audit current registered email, payments, source-control and CI, app-store, and secret-manager capabilities and public claims. Derive the integration inventory from the provider, DevOps and secret-manager registries. Include current delegated API-key, webhook, credential-check and AI workflow behavior without treating those paths as dedicated provider connectors. Cover credential boundaries, provider behavior, lifecycle safety, mocked contracts, and recent live evidence. Leave repository Pages routing to the edge shard.
